entities.summary: Lucius Coelius Antipater was a Roman jurist and historian who played a significant role in shaping the Roman legal system and leaving a lasting legacy in the annals of Roman history. Born in Rome, Italy, around 160 BCE, he was a contemporary of prominent figures such as C. Gracchus and L. Crassus, and was known for his expertise in Roman law. His most notable work, the 'Digest of Roman Law,' was a comprehensive compilation of Roman legal principles and was widely used as a reference by Roman jurists and scholars for centuries. Coelius Antipater's contributions to Roman law and history have been widely recognized, and he remains an important figure in the study of Roman law and culture. Despite his significant impact on Roman history, Coelius Antipater's life and legacy have been somewhat overshadowed by that of his more famous contemporaries, and he remains a relatively lesser-known figure in the annals of Roman history.
